quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: When turning left, you should:

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.explanation: A motorcycle leans to turn. Press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward to make the bike lean in that direction.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol was consumed

questions.explanation: BAC is affected by three main factors: how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Your gender, physical condition, and food intake may also matter. How often you drink does not affect your BAC.

questions.question: Small vehicles can look ______ away and seem to be going ______ than they really are.
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and slower than they actually are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their real distance and speed.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you from behind, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center of your lane.
Stay on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the passing vehicle can be dangerous.

questions.question: Motorcycle headlights are usually:

options.text: More powerful than a car's headlights.
Just as powerful as a car's headlights.
Not as powerful as a car's headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not as powerful as a car's headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are generally smaller and weaker than car headlights.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: In normal conditions, you should stay ______ behind the vehicle ahead of you.
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead in normal conditions. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: It is most important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: You need to slow down suddenly.
There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You need to slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's single brake light is less noticeable than a car's lights. Flash your brake light when slowing quickly so other drivers notice.

questions.question: When an operator's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing up, the operator:
questions.explanation: Operators use hand signals to show turns or stops. A left arm bent at the elbow and pointing up means the operator plans to turn right or change lanes right.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, a person age 21 or older with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ is legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Riding a motorcycle while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Is usually safe for motorcyclists, except when it is raining.
Should always be avoided because other parts of the lane do not have oil.
Helps most motorcycle tires grip the road better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcyclists, except when it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of the lane. When the road is dry, this area has enough grip for motorcyclists to ride safely. The strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can often ride to one side and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When someone is passing you, do not move to the far side of your lane because it:

options.text: Stops the passing driver from moving into your lane too soon.
Makes the passing driver want to move into your lane too soon.
Makes the passing driver want to finish the pass as quickly as possible.
Encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes the passing driver want to move into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane when being passed is dangerous. It might make the passing driver return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders rarely hear a tire going flat. You will notice it instead by how the motorcycle feels and handles.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks that run along the road, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks at a 90-degree angle.
Cross the tracks at a 45-degree angle or sharper.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the tracks at a 45-degree angle or sharper.
questions.explanation: To safely cross railroad tracks or road seams that run alongside your lane, move to a position where you can cross at least at a 45-degree angle. Then turn quickly and sharply. Trying to edge across slowly can catch your tires and throw you off balance.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should be positioned:

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front of the group, right behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without asking the newer rider to lead.

questions.question: When it is raining, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side and wait for the rain to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, the road is very slippery because oil from cars has not washed away. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is often the best choice, but this may vary.

questions.question: Who should set the pace in a group of riders?

options.text: The riders just behind the leader

questions.explanation: The last rider in the group should set the pace. This makes sure no one is left behind.

questions.question: When riding through curves, making turns, or entering a highway, the best group formation is:
questions.explanation: While a staggered formation is usually best for group riding, riders should form a single line when going through curves, making turns, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: A person may not have to wear a helmet while riding if:

options.text: They are 21 or older and have completed an approved Motorcycle Operator Training Course.
Never. A helmet must always be worn.
They have had no accidents for five years.
They have had no traffic violations for five years.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are 21 or older and have completed an approved Motorcycle Operator Training Course.
questions.explanation: In Texas, riders who are 21 or older do not need a helmet if they completed an approved Motorcycle Operator Training Course from the Department of Public Safety. They may also be exempt if they have medical insurance. All riders should wear a helmet for safety, even if not required.

questions.question: Court costs for a DWI conviction start at:
questions.explanation: A DWI conviction has many consequences. Court costs start at $70.
